AppliesTo.description: Scope as a set of candidate predicates over topology attributes. Candidates are not ranked.

entity_type.description: Type of entity the assertion binds to; 'site' for a workflow trigger.
entity_type.title: Entity Type

candidates.description: Every plausible scope from the first case: the stated condition plus one per origin attribute (model, firmware, install_year if not already present, site, region). Never the device ID unless the text limits it to that unit.
candidates.title: Candidates

decided.description: Set by an answer to the one question; null while undecided.

AppliesTo.title: AppliesTo

Candidate.description: One hypothesis for the assertion's scope, a predicate over topology attributes (contracts/predicates.md). The device ID is never a candidate: the device is the origin of the case in evidence.cases. Only if the text limits the rule to that unit ('only this one') is "id == 'X'" added. A candidate with against > 0 is eliminated.

edge.description: Open edge: 'open' when the stated condition is relative (condition_is_relative) and the predicate's number came from the origin node's attribute, not from the speaker. The number is then the newest value known to be in, not a boundary. Everything else is 'closed'. On a new entity an open <=/< candidate holds at or below its number, is unknown above it, and fails only for a missing attribute. A supporting case or a 'yes' answer on a newer entity raises the number; a 'no' answer closes the edge at the current number. Never invent a margin.
edge.title: Edge

support.description: Number of cases (not sources) whose entity satisfied this predicate.
support.title: Support

against.description: Number of cases whose entity failed this predicate, or failed outcomes where it held. > 0 eliminates the candidate.
against.title: Against

basis.description: One sentence: where this candidate came from (speaker's words or the origin's attribute).
basis.title: Basis

Candidate.title: Candidate

Case.description: A distinct incident: entity plus time. Chat and email about the same incident (same entity, same day) are one case.

entity.description: Node or site ID the case happened on (the origin, for the first case).
entity.title: Entity

outcome.description: 'recovered' from a thread confirmation ('traffic is back') or a telemetry event; 'failed' if the action did not work; null if not reported.
outcome.title: Outcome

Case.title: Case

Decided.description: The predicate a human answer (or evidence leaving one) fixed. Other candidates stay recorded but are not evaluated.

edge.description: Edge of the decided predicate, carried over from the option chosen.
edge.title: Edge

Decided.title: Decided

Evidence.description: Provenance. cases are distinct incidents (entity + time); sources are documents. Erkki's chat and email are one case, two sources. support counts cases.

excerpt.description: Copied character for character from the source; re-verified as a substring after whitespace normalisation.
excerpt.title: Excerpt

said_by_role.description: Role of the speaker of the rule.
said_by_role.title: Said By Role

said_by.description: Name of the speaker of the rule; the one question and the notification go to this person.
said_by.title: Said By

Evidence.title: Evidence

Trigger.description: When the assertion applies. kind 'incident': event plus every listed symptom must be present (checks the agent runs against telemetry). kind 'workflow': event only, e.g. 'dispatch_created' with the site as entity; the barrier key is a workflow trigger with action 'site.access_key' and action_text holding the key location.

symptoms.description: All must be present for an incident trigger to match. Empty for a workflow trigger.
symptoms.title: Symptoms

Trigger.title: Trigger

description: A context assertion: a reusable operational rule captured from a conversation. Nothing is ever deleted.

action_text.description: The action in the speaker's words. For a value-carrying action (site.access_key) this is the fact itself, e.g. where the key is.
action_text.title: Action Text

trust.description: Derived deterministically, first rule that applies: (1) any case with outcome 'recovered' -> verified_by_outcome; (2) hedged -> hunch; (3) said_by_role == expert or first_hand -> stated; (4) otherwise hunch. A field engineer reporting what he did or saw on site is 'stated'. Trust and support are separate axes.
trust.title: Trust

status.description: open: candidates undecided; decided: answered or evidence left one; disputed: conflicts with another assertion; review: an outcome contradicted it.
status.title: Status

questions_asked.description: Question keys (contracts/get_context.md). A key is appended once and never removed.
questions_asked.title: Questions Asked

supersedes.description: ID of the assertion this one replaced. Set only by the supersede rule (BACKEND_PROMPT 5.2) for value-carrying actions.
supersedes.title: Supersedes

superseded_by.description: ID of the assertion that replaced this one. Set only by the supersede rule, together with valid_to. Nothing is ever deleted.
superseded_by.title: Superseded By

recorded_at.description: When the system learned it (ingestion time).
recorded_at.title: Recorded At

valid_while.description: Stated end condition, stored as text only. Nothing evaluates it (pending).
valid_while.title: Valid While

title: Assertion
